name: Cleopatra
info: Cleopatra VII Thea Philopator (69–30 BCE) was Queen of the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt from 51 BCE and its last active ruler, who allied herself with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony and died as Octavian made Egypt a Roman province.

facts.born: Early 69 BCE (or 70 BCE) in Alexandria; daughter of Ptolemy XII Auletes of the Macedonian Greek Ptolemaic dynasty and an uncertain mother, presumably Cleopatra V Tryphaena
facts.died: 10 or 12 August 30 BCE in Alexandria, aged 39, by suicide, probably by poison; whether in the palace or in her tomb is unclear
facts.role: Regent for her father from 31 May 52 BCE; Queen of the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt, 51–30 BCE, reigning in turn with her brothers Ptolemy XIII and Ptolemy XIV and her son Caesarion
facts.known: The last active Hellenistic pharaoh; her alliances with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony; the only Ptolemaic ruler known to have learned Egyptian; the Donations of Alexandria; the defeat at Actium; her suicide; a hostile Roman tradition and a long afterlife in art

t: Cleopatra inherited in 51 BCE a kingdom indebted to Rome, lost a civil war to her brother Ptolemy XIII, and was restored by Julius Caesar in 47 BCE.
With Mark Antony she regained former Ptolemaic lands in the Levant, Cyprus and Cyrene, and in 34 BCE the Donations of Alexandria named her children rulers of the east.
Octavian declared war on her, won at Actium in 31 BCE and invaded Egypt in 30 BCE; she killed herself, and Egypt became a Roman province.
dyk: A papyrus of 33 BCE granting tax exemptions to a Roman ends, in a different hand, with the Greek word for "make it happen"; it is possibly Cleopatra's own autograph.
ev: Cleopatra is born to Ptolemy XII Auletes, probably in the early part of the year
Her father dies and she begins her reign, at first alongside her brother Ptolemy XIII
Driven from Alexandria by her brother's party, she returns with an army and meets Julius Caesar in the palace
Ptolemy XIII drowns in the Nile, Caesar makes her joint ruler with Ptolemy XIV, and she gives birth to Caesarion
She sails to Tarsos to meet Mark Antony, who follows her to Alexandria
At the Donations of Alexandria she and her children are declared rulers of lands under Antony's authority
Octavian's fleet under Agrippa defeats hers and Antony's at the Battle of Actium
Octavian takes Alexandria; Antony and then Cleopatra commit suicide

sections.early:
Cleopatra VII was born in early 69 BCE to Ptolemy XII Auletes and an uncertain mother, presumably his wife Cleopatra V Tryphaena. She belonged to the Macedonian Greek Ptolemaic dynasty, descended from Ptolemy I Soter, a general and companion of Alexander the Great. The Ptolemies were crowned at Memphis but lived in the largely Greek city of Alexandria and refused to learn Egyptian; Cleopatra, whose first language was Koine Greek, is the only one known to have learned it, and Plutarch implies she spoke several other languages. Her childhood tutor was Philostratos, and she presumably studied at the Musaeum.

Roman intervention in Egypt predated her reign. Ptolemy XI had willed the kingdom to Rome as collateral for loans, and her father kept his throne by lavish gifts to Roman statesmen such as Pompey and Julius Caesar, which bankrupted him. When Rome annexed Cyprus in 58 BCE and drove his brother to suicide, Ptolemy XII was exiled from Egypt and went to Rome, ostensibly accompanied by Cleopatra, then about 11. Her older sister Berenice IV ruled in his place.

In the spring of 55 BCE the Roman governor of Syria, Aulus Gabinius, persuaded by Pompey with an offer of 10,000 talents, invaded Egypt and restored Ptolemy XII; the young cavalry officer Mark Antony served under him. Ptolemy XII executed Berenice and her wealthy supporters. He made a will naming Cleopatra and Ptolemy XIII his joint heirs, and on 31 May 52 BCE made Cleopatra his regent, as an inscription at Dendera indicates. His unpaid debts passed to his heirs, who owed the Roman Republic 17.5 million drachmas.
sections.rise:
Ptolemy XII died some time before 22 March 51 BCE. Cleopatra faced famine caused by drought and a low Nile flood, and lawlessness among the Gabiniani, the Roman soldiers Gabinius had left in Egypt. By 29 August 51 BCE official documents listed her as sole ruler, without her brother Ptolemy XIII. He kept powerful allies, the eunuch Potheinos, the tutor Theodotus of Chios and the commander Achillas, and by the autumn of 50 BCE had the upper hand. Cleopatra was forced to flee Alexandria; by the spring of 48 BCE she was in Roman Syria gathering an army, and she camped outside Pelousion when her brother's forces blocked her return.

After his defeat at Pharsalus, Pompey sought refuge in Egypt, and Ptolemy XIII had him stabbed to death near Pelousion on 28 September 48 BCE. Caesar arrived in Alexandria and called on the siblings to reconcile. Cleopatra came to him in person: Cassius Dio says she charmed him with her wit, while Plutarch alleges she was smuggled into the palace in a bed sack. Potheinos sent Achillas with an army of 20,000 against Caesar's 4,000, and Caesar and Cleopatra were besieged in the palace into 47 BCE.

Reinforcements lifted the siege early that year, and Ptolemy XIII drowned while fleeing by boat. Caesar appointed the 12-year-old Ptolemy XIV joint ruler with the 22-year-old Cleopatra, who gave birth to Caesarion some time in 47 BCE and repeatedly declared Caesar the father. She was in Rome when Caesar was assassinated on 15 March 44 BCE. A few months later Ptolemy XIV died, allegedly poisoned by her, and she made Caesarion her co-ruler.
sections.deeds:
In the Liberators' civil war Cleopatra sent the four legions Caesar had left in Egypt to Dolabella and took her own fleet towards Greece, though a storm kept it from the fighting. In 41 BCE Mark Antony, master of the eastern half of the Roman world, summoned her to Tarsos; she sailed up the Kydnos in the royal barge and entertained him for two nights of banquets. He visited Alexandria that winter, and by the end of 40 BCE she had borne him twins, Alexander Helios and Cleopatra Selene II. A third child, Ptolemy Philadelphus, was born in 36 BCE.

Antony had the authority to restore former Ptolemaic lands. Cilicia and Cyprus were hers by 38 BCE, and at Antioch she received nearly all of Phoenicia, Ptolemais Akko, Coele-Syria, the region around Jericho, part of the Nabataean Kingdom and Cyrene. She gave Antony 200 ships in 40 BCE and brought funds and clothing for his troops after his Parthian campaign of 36 BCE failed with the loss of some 30,000 men. In 34 BCE, at the Donations of Alexandria, she dressed as Isis and was declared Queen of Kings beside Caesarion as King of Kings, and her children by Antony were named rulers of Armenia, Media, Parthia, Syria, Cilicia, Crete and Cyrene.

At home she ruled as an absolute monarch, the sole lawgiver and chief religious authority. She oversaw the building of temples to Egyptian and Greek gods and of the Caesareum of Alexandria, and ordered the royal granaries to feed the starving during drought. Apparent financial troubles led her to debase her coinage. She was the only Ptolemaic queen to issue coins on her own behalf.
sections.opponents:
Cleopatra's first enemies were in her own family. Ptolemy XIII's court drove her out, and her sister Arsinoe IV was declared queen by the army besieging the palace; in 41 BCE Cleopatra convinced Antony to have Arsinoe executed at Ephesus, and to hand over her defecting governor of Cyprus, Serapion, for execution. Herod of Judea, whose kingdom covered former Ptolemaic territory she wished to reclaim, became a rival, and Malichus I of Nabatea later burned her fleet. In Rome, Cicero, who met her at Caesar's villa, found her arrogant and wrote of her unfavourably.

Her most effective opponent was Octavian. He exploited Roman feeling against the empowerment of a foreign queen at the Republic's expense, accusing Antony in the Senate of being a slave to his Oriental queen. In the propaganda war that began in late 34 BCE she was said to have brainwashed Antony with witchcraft, and Pliny the Elder claims she dissolved a costly pearl in vinegar to win a bet. When Antony's will was made public, Rome declared war on Cleopatra, not on Antony. Her insistence on taking part in the campaign led prominent Romans such as Ahenobarbus and Plancus to defect.

Partisan Roman writers later accused her of cowardly deserting Antony at Actium, and a report that she tested poisons on prisoners and servants is most likely pro-Octavian propaganda. The Augustan poets Virgil, Horace, Propertius and Ovid perpetuated the regime's negative view. Among modern historians, Ronald Syme asserted that she was of little importance to Caesar and that Octavian's propaganda magnified her to an excessive degree.
sections.last:
On 2 September 31 BCE Octavian's fleet under Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa met Antony and Cleopatra's at Actium. Cleopatra, commanding 60 ships at the rear, sailed through the fighting in a withdrawal to the Peloponnese, and Antony followed her. Mass defections to Octavian followed. Back in Egypt she prepared to leave the throne to Caesarion and sail from the Red Sea to a foreign port, perhaps in India, but Malichus I of Nabatea burned her fleet. She negotiated with Octavian, asking that her children inherit Egypt and that Antony be allowed to live there in exile.

Octavian invaded in the spring of 30 BCE. On 1 August Antony's fleet and cavalry surrendered. Cleopatra hid in her tomb and sent word to Antony that she had killed herself; in despair he stabbed himself, and according to Plutarch was brought to her still dying. Octavian's companion Proculeius entered the tomb and detained her. According to Livy she told Octavian, "I will not be led in a triumph."

Informed by a spy that she and her children would be moved to Rome in three days, she prepared for suicide. She died on 12 August 30 BCE, aged 39, and her servants Eiras and Charmion also took their lives. The popular belief is that she let an asp or Egyptian cobra bite her; Plutarch relates this but suggests a toxin scratched in with an implement, Dio a needle, and Strabo an ointment. No snake was found with her body. Octavian had her buried beside Antony. Caesarion, sent away to Upper Egypt, returned on a promise of recognition as king and was executed around 29 August. Octavian made Egypt a Roman province.
sections.legacy:
The fall of the Ptolemaic Kingdom marked the end of the Hellenistic period, which had begun with the death of Alexander in 323 BCE. Cleopatra's three children by Antony were sent to Rome in the care of Octavia. Cleopatra Selene II married Juba II and ruled Mauretania with him; their son Ptolemy, executed by Caligula in 40 CE, was the last known monarch of the dynasty. A cult of Cleopatra still existed in Egypt as late as 373 CE.

Almost 50 ancient Roman works mention her, often tersely and with Augustan propaganda about her failings. Plutarch's Life of Antonius, written in the 1st century CE, is the most thorough surviving account; Josephus and Cassius Dio add to it, while material giving her own point of view, on coins and papyri, is very limited. Though commonly seen as a seductress, she had only two known partners, Caesar and Antony, and Plutarch credits her with a strong personality and charming wit more than with beauty. Her command of naval forces and her administrative acts go largely unnoticed.

Medieval and Renaissance literature inherited the critical Roman view, which Bernardino Cacciante challenged in 1504. William Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra, largely based on Plutarch, premiered in 1608. Since the Victorian era she has been an icon of Egyptomania, portrayed in film by Theda Bara (1917), Claudette Colbert (1934) and Elizabeth Taylor (1963). Michael Grant argues that she probably had no Egyptian ancestry and "would have described herself as Greek"; Duane W. Roller speculates that her mother may have been half Egyptian.

summary: The last active ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt, Cleopatra kept her throne and enlarged her kingdom through alliances with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony. Defeated with Antony at Actium by Octavian, she killed herself in 30 BCE, and Egypt became a Roman province. Roman writers left a hostile portrait that later ages reworked.
